The company frames adoption through three pillars:

1. **"AI visibility & control"** – Employees gain insight into usage patterns and compliance
2. **"AI Adoption"** – Teams receive training and support at the moment of need
3. **"Contextual AI assistance"** – Workers access proactive next-best-action recommendations

Key quote on implementation approach:
**"educate employees about how to use AI, without stifling innovation"** (attributed to Patrick Fueldner, IT Product Manager)

## Targeted Language

- **"in the context of how they're using these applications"** (workflow-embedded training)
- **"contextual AI assistance for every workflow"** (personalization element)
- **"reaching them in the moment of need"** (just-in-time support)

## Target Buyer

Enterprise IT/Digital Adoption leaders responsible for governance, compliance, and change management during AI tool rollouts. Secondary audience: HR/organizational development teams managing workforce readiness.

Base directory for this skill: /home/node/.claude/skills/agent-browser

# Browser Automation with agent-browser

## Quick start

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # Navigate to page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # Get interactive elements with refs
agent-browser click @e1         # Click element by ref
agent-browser fill @e2 "text"   # Fill input by ref
agent-browser close             # Close browser
```

## Core workflow

1. Navigate: `agent-browser open <url>`
2. Snapshot: `agent-browser snapshot -i` (returns elements with refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
3. Interact using refs from the snapshot
4. Re-snapshot after navigation or significant DOM changes

## Commands

### Navigation

```bash
agent-browser open <url>      # Navigate to URL
agent-browser back            # Go back
agent-browser forward         # Go forward
agent-browser reload          # Reload page
agent-browser close           # Close browser
```

### Snapshot (page analysis)

```bash
agent-browser snapshot            # Full accessibility tree
agent-browser snapshot -i         # Interactive elements only (recommended)
agent-browser snapshot -c         # Compact output
agent-browser snapshot -d 3       # Limit depth to 3
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main" # Scope to CSS selector
```

### Interactions (use @refs from snapshot)

```bash
agent-browser click @e1           # Click
agent-browser dblclick @e1        # Double-click
agent-browser fill @e2 "text"     # Clear and type
agent-browser type @e2 "text"     # Type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter         # Press key
agent-browser hover @e1           # Hover
agent-browser check @e1           # Check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e1         # Uncheck checkbox
agent-browser select @e1 "value"  # Select dropdown option
agent-browser scroll down 500     # Scroll page
agent-browser upload @e1 file.pdf # Upload files
```

### Get information

```bash
agent-browser get text @e1        # Get element text
agent-browser get html @e1        # Get innerHTML
agent-browser get value @e1       # Get input value
agent-browser get attr @e1 href   # Get attribute
agent-browser get title           # Get page title
agent-browser get url             # Get current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"   # Count matching elements
```

### Screenshots & PDF

```bash
agent-browser screenshot          # Save to temp directory
agent-browser screenshot path.png # Save to specific path
agent-browser screenshot --full   # Full page
agent-browser pdf output.pdf      # Save as PDF
```

### Wait

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # Wait for element
agent-browser wait 2000                    # Wait milliseconds
agent-browser wait --text "Success"        # Wait for text
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"    # Wait for URL pattern
agent-browser wait --load networkidle      # Wait for network idle
```

### Semantic locators (alternative to refs)

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
```

### Authentication with saved state

```bash
# Login once
agent-browser open https://app.example.com/login
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser fill @e1 "username"
agent-browser fill @e2 "password"
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"
agent-browser state save auth.json

# Later: load saved state
agent-browser state load auth.json
agent-browser open https://app.example.com/dashboard
```

### Cookies & Storage

```bash
agent-browser cookies                     # Get all cookies
agent-browser cookies set name value      # Set cookie
agent-browser cookies clear               # Clear cookies
agent-browser storage local               # Get localStorage
agent-browser storage local set k v       # Set value
```

### JavaScript

```bash
agent-browser eval "document.title"   # Run JavaScript
```

## Example: Form submission

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com/form
agent-browser snapshot -i
# Output shows: textbox "Email" [ref=e1], textbox "Password" [ref=e2], button "Submit" [ref=e3]

agent-browser fill @e1 "user@example.com"
agent-browser fill @e2 "password123"
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i  # Check result
```

## Example: Data extraction

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com/products
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser get text @e1  # Get product title
agent-browser get attr @e2 href  # Get link URL
agent-browser screenshot products.png
```

Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming organizations across almost every industry, offering untold opportunities for efficiency, productivity and innovation. However, AI adoption often fails—not because of the technology itself, but due to human barriers such as resistance, uncertainty and lack of alignment among employees. Many organizations focus solely on implementing AI tools without preparing their workforce, leading to poor adoption and wasted investment. In fact, an independent study into personal, team and organizatio nal AI usage co nducted by Prosci, surveying 1,107 professionals across multiple industries, found that 63% of organizations cite human factors as a primary challenge in AI implementation. Yet, when implemented effectively, GenAI adoption is perceived to drive a number of benefits; the same study revealed that 61% of respondents believed it would make projects more successful, 65% thought it would boost their personal success, and 73% said their organizations would be more successful as a result of GenAI adoption. Top Perceived Benefits of GenAI Adoption By taking a people-first appro ach to enterprise AI adoption —foc using on communication, training and leadership support—companies can help their people by preparing, supporting and equipping them to adopt this exciting new technology. In this article, we explore key insights from Prosci’s research on AI adoption, why a people-first approach is essential, and how a structured approach to change management can help your organization integrate AI effectively and sustainably. × AI implementation vs. AI adoption While AI implementation and AI adoption are often used interchangeably, they are not the same. Implementation is the technical process—installing AI tools, integrating them into systems, and making them available for use. Adoption , however, is about people. It’s the process of ensuring AI becomes a natural, effective part of everyday work. Many organizations invest heavily in AI technology but struggle to embed it into workflows. The challenge isn’t the technology itself, but the human response to it. Factors such as fear of job displacement, lack of AI training, and mistrust of AI decisions can cause employees to feel uncertain, hesitant, or even resistant to the change. When these concerns go unaddressed, AI adoption stalls. This is why a people-first approach is essential. AI adoption succeeds when organizations focus on supporting employees, building mutual trust, and ensuring they have the knowledge and confidence to use AI effectively. When people feel equipped and empowered, they engage with AI instead of resisting it. According to MIT Sloan , over 60% of companies with more than 10,000 employees have already adopted AI, highlighting its growing role in large-scale operations. As AI becomes increasingly integrated into business processes, organizations that prioritize a human-centric approach to managing this change will be best positioned for long-term success. # Change Management + AI Platforms for Employees — Research Findings (2025-2026)

## Bottom line up front
Two platforms stand out, and they occupy **opposite ends** of the "AI companion for change adoption" spectrum:

- **Prosci Kaiya** — the change-management *methodology leader's* AI, but it's an assistant **for the change practitioner**, not for the individual employee going through the change.
- **WalkMe (SAP) / WalkMeX** — the one that actually **walks each individual employee through a new system in the flow of work**, in real time, on their own screen. This is the closest thing to a 1:1 AI companion for change adoption — but it's positioned as a technical "adoption layer," not an emotional companion.

**Neither** frames a *personal, named 1:1 AI companion that emotionally walks each individual employee through adopting a specific change.* That white space is real. WalkMe owns the mechanics of it; nobody owns the human/companion framing of it.

---

## 1. Prosci Kaiya — STRONGEST on change-management authority, but practitioner-facing

**What it is:** A generative-AI assistant trained on Prosci's 25+ years of change-management research (ADKAR, 3-Phase Process), built for change practitioners and leaders.
**URL:** https://www.prosci.com/kaiya-ai-tool · https://www.prosci.com/ai-change-management

### Verbatim hero copy
> **"Your Expert AI Change Management Assistant."**
> **"Access insights and solutions for any change management initiative. Kaiya saves you time, scales your impact, and accelerates change."**

> **"Ask any question. Kaiya has the answer."**
> **"We built Kaiya to empower change practitioners and leaders. With its on-demand support, all you have to do is ask Kaiya a question, and it will help you power through day-to-day change management tasks so you can focus your time where it matters most — on the people side of change."**

> **"Accelerate your work. Kaiya is your assistant for any change or transformation task, on-demand and ready to answer any questions on change you have."**

Use cases listed verbatim: *"Build guided ADKAR blueprints · Draft key change messages · Customize communication for different audiences · Create sponsorship strategies · Develop resistance management tactics."*

### The "companion" language it DOES use (but note who for)
> **"Easy to Adopt. Our intuitive interface is designed to feel like you're talking to an expert. Talk to Kaiya like you would an exceptionally smart colleague."**

A beta-user testimonial (verbatim):
> **"It's a coach that's always there that I can reach out to anytime. Having Kaiya available to me has improved my confidence and gives me piece of mind..."**

That "coach that's always there" line is the closest Kaiya gets to companion framing — but the "me" is the **change manager**, not the employee living through the change.

### Story frame
Prosci's narrative is **"implementation vs. adoption"** and **"people-first"**:
> **"AI adoption often fails—not because of the technology itself, but due to human barriers such as resistance, uncertainty and lack of alignment among employees."**
> **"Implementation is the technical process... Adoption, however, is about people. It's the process of ensuring AI becomes a natural, effective part of everyday work."**
> **"By taking a people-first approach to enterprise AI adoption—focusing on communication, training and leadership support—companies can help their people by preparing, supporting and equipping them..."**

### Emotional / strategic angle
Authority and de-risking. The pitch is: change fails because of *humans*, and Prosci owns the science of the human side. Kaiya = that expertise, on demand. Data-point framing: *"65% of change practitioners agree they will be more successful using AI than those who don't."*

### Buyer
**The change practitioner / change leader / Head of Change** (and the Prosci Membership or enterprise-license buyer). Explicit: *"We built Kaiya to empower change practitioners and leaders."* Not CHRO/CIO-targeted in the copy; it's for the change-management function itself.

### Does it walk each individual employee 1:1 through a change? 
**No.** It's a productivity/expertise tool *for the person managing the change*. It helps a practitioner draft the plan that will move employees — it does not sit beside the employee. (The OCM Solution review confirms: *"designed for change management professionals and practitioners... not for end-user employee engagement."*)

---

## 2. WalkMe (SAP) / WalkMeX — CLOSEST to a 1:1 companion that walks each employee through change

**What it is:** A Digital Adoption Platform (now SAP-owned) with an AI layer (WalkMeX) that overlays any application and guides employees, step-by-step, through workflows and new-system changes in real time, on their own screen.
**URL:** https://www.walkme.com/ · https://www.walkme.com/solutions/use-case/ai-transformation/

### Verbatim hero copy
> **"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."**
> **"WalkMe is the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work."**

AI-transformation page:
> **"AI transformation, without the friction."**
> **"Turn AI promise into business reality."**
> **"Successful AI transformation is more than getting a chatbot live."**

### The 1:1 / in-the-flow-of-work language (this is the key differentiator)
Verbatim capability copy:
> **"Omnipresent contextual AI assistance."**
> **"reads the screen and understands what needs to happen next."**
> **"AI follows the work wherever it goes."**
> **"guid[ing] them through every workflow, inside the tools they already use."**
> Section headers: **"AI that follows the work"** and **"From answers to execution."**

Its stated adoption pillars, verbatim: **"AI visibility & control," "AI Adoption"** (*"Teams receive training and support at the moment of need"*), and **"Contextual AI assistance"** (*"proactive next-best-action recommendations"*), delivered **"in the context of how they're using these applications"** and **"reaching them in the moment of need."**

### Story frame — how they narrate walking an employee through change
WalkMe's frame is **screen-level, real-time, per-employee guidance**: the AI *sees the individual's screen*, knows the individual's next step, and **walks that specific person through the new system live, without pulling them out of their work.** This is mechanically the "1:1 companion walking each employee through a change" — WalkMe literally overlays guidance on the individual employee's screen as they hit the new tool.

### Emotional / strategic angle
**Friction removal + ROI proof.** Not warm/human — it's operational: *"You bought AI for every employee"* (the "Prove" section), *"license optimization,"* *"from answers to execution."* The emotion it sells to the buyer is *relief from failed rollouts*, not companionship for the employee.

### Buyer
**Primary: IT / CIO** (measuring AI adoption, proving ROI, license optimization). **Secondary: HR / org-development, plus Sales & Customer Care leaders.** Enterprise digital-adoption owners. Note: the copy attributes voice to an *"IT Product Manager"* — a very IT-led sale.

### Does it walk each individual employee 1:1 through a change?
**Yes — mechanically, this is the closest of anyone.** WalkMeX rides on the individual's screen and guides *that person* through the new workflow in real time. But it's framed as a *contextual adoption layer / co-pilot for software*, **not** as a personal, named, emotionally-present companion. The "in the flow of work," "moment of need," "follows the work wherever it goes" language is exactly the 1:1-guidance territory — delivered as utility, not relationship.

---

## The gap (directly answers your key question)
- **Prosci Kaiya** = deepest change-management *credibility* and the richest "people-first / adoption-not-implementation" narrative — but the AI serves the **practitioner**, one level removed from the employee.
- **WalkMe** = the only one that literally **sits with each individual employee and walks them through the new system in real time** — but framed as cold IT infrastructure ("the critical layer"), not a companion.

**No 2025-2026 platform combines the two:** a *personal, named 1:1 AI companion* that (a) carries genuine change-management/people-first methodology AND (b) emotionally walks *each individual employee* through adopting a specific change, keeping their context and identity. WalkMe owns the *mechanism*; Prosci owns the *methodology and human framing*; the *companion* framing for the individual employee is unclaimed.
